newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 18.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
RESIGNATION OF CONGRESS PARLIAMENTARY PARTY CHIEF IMMINENT

The exit of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao as the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) leader appeared imminent to senior party leaders who began the search for a successor. While there was consensus on Rao's exit, the search for his successor appeared difficult. Congress chief Sitaram Kesri's aides spoke to senior leaders seeking support for Kesri to become the CPP leader. They said that there should not be two centres of power. However, senior party leaders Sharad Pawar and Vijaybhaskara Reddy, both contenders for the CPP post, wanted a member of the Lok Sabha (Lower House) to succeed Narasimha Rao.
Indian Express
GOVERNMENT BUGNLING LED TO WHEAT CRISIS

The government's decision to import two million tonnes of wheat has created a flutter in the Food Ministry. Ministry officials claimed that according to current estimates, stocks for the Public Distribution System (PDS) stood at 8.4 million tonnes, enough to last until May 1997. Sources said the existing stocks did not warrant such immediate imports. Questions were also raised about the government's claim that it needed to import wheat to maintain prescribed buffer levels. Sources said the government kept exporting wheat until June 1996, despite warning signals in March that there was no surplus.
The Times Of India
NON-FOREST ACTIVITIES BANNED IN FOREST AREAS

The Supreme Court banned all non-forest activities including saw mills, veneer or ply wood mills and mining in the forest areas. It also prohibited transportation of timber or wood by any means from forests. In an interim order the court directed all state governments to set up expert committees within one month. These committees would assess the sustainable capacity of the forests regarding saw mills and timber-based industries.
The Economic Times
JOINT VENTURE ENVISAGES INDIA AS TRAFFIC HUB

Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) and British Telecom (BT) proposed to form a 15 billion rupee joint venture to make India a hub for international traffic. The joint venture proposed to amalgamate all international traffic to Britain from the Middle East, South Asia and South East Asia in India. It would then be transmitted to and received from Britian. Sources said this would lead to economies of scale and would allow BT to offer cheaper rates to the long distance carriers of these countries.
SHALLOW INDUSTRIAL GROWTH IN FIRST HALF

Industrial growth rate for 24 leading industries during April-October 1996 suffered an alarming dip to 4.8 percent compared to 12 percent recorded in the corresponding period last year. The rate, however, improved marginally against April-September 1996 level of 3.2 percent. Official sources said with this growth rate, the gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate would be 5.5 to 5.8 percent in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). The performance of power, coal, crude production and saleable steel was lower than expected during April-October this year.
KIER STAKE IN ISPAT GROUP COAL ARM

Kier International Ltd, a UK-based mining company, is planning to pick up a stake in Ispat group's captive coal mine company, Bhadrawati Coal Company. It would be the sole fuel sourcing agent for the Bhadrawati power project in Maharashtra. The Bhadrawati power project, which would have a generating capacity of 1,150 megawatts, is one of the eight fast-track power projects which are awaiting the government's nod for counter-guarantee. Company officials said the matter was pending with the Power Ministry.
Financial Express
BANK CREDIT TO INDUSTRY FALLS BY 2.77 BLN RUPEES

The banking sector's credit to business and industry fell by 2.77 billion rupees during the fortnight ending November 22. It was an unusual development. Although there has been deceleration in the off-take of non-food credit fortnight after fortnight during the busy season, it was the first time that the commercial credit flowed back to the commercial banks.
MEGA CORPORATES MOPPING UP OWN SHARES ON THE SLY

Mega corporates started buying back their own shares in anticipation of the Companies Act being amended in the next few months. Market sources said Reliance, Bajaj Auto, Gujarat Ambuja, Great Eastern Shipping, Bombay Dyeing, Raymond, Sundaram Finance and other companies had been buying their own shares through a subtle operation over the last few days. Sources said Reliance had bought nearly five percent of its own equity capital from the market. Similarly, Bajaj Auto reportedly picked up over half a million shares.
OIL MAJOR PLANS MEGA PUBLIC ISSUE EARLY NEXT YEAR

The Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) plans its mega public issue of around 20 billion rupees early next year. The issue would not exceed 10 percent of IOC's paid-up capital, consisting of 380 million shares at a face-value of 10 rupees each. The IOC scrip is quoting at 625 rupees and at this price the 10 percent initial public offering would work out to 25 billion rupees. IOC also proposes to invest an additional 120 million rupee equity in Indo Mobil, a 50:50 joint venture between Mobil and U.S. with a paid-up capital of 200 million rupees.
The Observer
PROFIT MAKING BANKS TO BE GIVEN AUTONOMY

The Finance Ministry has asked the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), to submit a detailed scheme before December 31. On the basis of this scheme greater autonomy would be accorded to profit-making public sector banks. RBI sources said the apex bank was asked to prepare a report on the performance and financial standing of all 27 public sector banks. RBI's assessment report would be used to make sure that stronger banks enjoyed more autonomy in decision-making.
REVIVAL OF FORWARD TRADING ON CARDS

The Finance Ministry is contemplating the revival of forward trading in the stock market to rejuvenate the capital market. Sources in the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India said a few new components would be incorporated into the forward trading system to safeguard the interest of small investors.
Business Line
TWO FORD OUTFITS TO SET UP PLANTS IN TAMIL NADU

Two subsidiaries of Ford Motor Company, manufacturing auto components, are to set up production facilities near Madras in Tamil Nadu with a total investment of about $60 million. The plants are to come up close to the site where Mahindra Ford India Ltd, the joint venture between Mahindra & Mahindra and Ford Motor, is setting up its greenfield plant to manufacture Ford's Fiesta cars. The two subsidiaries, the Automotive Components Division and the Electronic Fuel Handling Division, would manufacture a range of products including instrument panels, air conditioners, alternators and electronic fuel handling systems.
Business Standard
BHARTI TELEVENTURES PUTS OFF ITS ADR ISSUE

Bharti Televentures Ltd (BTL) postponed its proposed $100 million American depository receipt (ADR) issue. Instead of approaching the ADR market in January or February next year, promoters of the Bharti group, the Mittals, decided to tap it in mid-1997. Company sources said BTL wanted to include its financial results of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) while going to the market. This would result in a higher level of confidence among investors, sources added.
